key_insight: Pressure can be treated as a geometric potential that curves an effective fluid space, making vortex-identification methods interpretable as curvature-based invariants.
engineering_relevance: This offers a unified mathematical lens for flow diagnostics and may improve how engineers interpret pressure-driven structures in turbulent and 2D flows.
method: Build a Newton-Cartan geometric framework for the flow field.
Apply a conformal transformation to map pressure into an effective spatial curvature.
Relate vortex criteria to Ricci/Einstein-like curvature tensors and geodesics.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical derivation linking the geodesic equation, Euler equation, and pressure Poisson equation, but does not report numerical experiments or benchmark data.
watch_item: The framework is largely theoretical, so practical use will depend on how robustly the curvature-based quantities can be computed from noisy simulation or experimental data.
paper_title: On the relationships between pressure geometrization and vortex identification
